text: Overview The ideas of Karl Marx, Friedrich Nietzsche and Sigmund Freud are particularly relevant to understanding the modern world. text: In addition to testability and falsifiability (ala Karl Popper), several other principles pertain to evaluating a scientific theory or hypothesis. These principles would be part of a more comprehensive approach to the "demarcation problem" (what distinguishes science from non-science). title: Other philosophers of science
text: Karl Popper (1902–1994) proposed falsifiability as the criterion of demarcation of science from nonscience. title: The Grand Inquisitor says that humans crave security and certainty more than truth and freedom
text: I am not sure I did a great job explaining the relevance of the "The Grand Inquisitor” to our course. In the novel, the skeptical brother Ivan tells this story to his younger brother Alyosha, who is a novice monk. The setting is sixteenth-century Seville, at the height of the Spanish Inquisition. Christ returns to earth silently and begins performing miracles. The people recognize him. They are drawn to him immediately. But the Grand Inquisitor, a powerful cardinal, has Christ arrested. That night, the Inquisitor visits Christ in his cell and delivers a long monologue. Christ says nothing. The Inquisitor explains that Christ made a fatal mistake in giving human beings freedom.
